summary: OrbitCraft is an interactive web-based space mission design simulator built to help students experience the real-world engineering trade-offs behind planning a spaceflight from concept to operation. In traditional classrooms, concepts like delta-v budgets, power-to-mass ratios, launch vehicle selection, and orbital constraints often remain abstract equations. OrbitCraft turns these constraints into hands-on gameplay where players design a custom spacecraft, select scientific instruments, allocate limited mass and power budgets, and choose a launch vehicle suited for their target orbit. Using real NASA mission parameters and orbital mechanics principles, the simulator immediately evaluates how each engineering decision affects mission feasibility, communication bandwidth, and scientific return. By allowing learners to iterate through failures and optimize competing subsystems, OrbitCraft bridges the gap between theoretical aerospace physics and practical systems engineering.
details:
OrbitCraft is an interactive space mission design and simulation game created for the "Space Mission Design Game" challenge. Players act as Lead Systems Engineers tasked with executing a complete space mission—such as a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Earth-observation satellite or a lunar reconnaissance orbiter—within strict budget, mass, and power limits.

Gameplay is structured into four sequential engineering phases:

  1. Mission & Orbit Selection: Players choose a target destination and scientific objective, which sets baseline delta-v ($\Delta v$), radiation, and communication distance requirements.
  2. Subsystem & Payload Configuration: Players balance scientific instruments against bus components (solar arrays, batteries, reaction wheels, and transceivers). Adding high-resolution instruments increases scientific score but consumes mass and electrical power.
  3. Launch Vehicle Integration: Players match their spacecraft's total wet mass against realistic payload-to-orbit capacities and launch costs.
  4. Mission Simulation & Trade-Off Evaluation: A physics-based simulation calculates net power margin, link budget, orbital insertion success, and overall mission score, highlighting exact bottlenecks (e.g., power deficit during eclipse or insufficient $\Delta v$) so players can redesign and re-fly.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Aerospace engineering relies heavily on coupled trade-offs where optimizing one parameter degrades another. OrbitCraft makes these invisible constraints tangible for high school and undergraduate students, encouraging systems-level thinking, iterative problem-solving, and intuitive understanding of spacecraft engineering without requiring advanced astrodynamics software.

Tools, Languages & Development Factors

  • Tech Stack: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (for interactive UI sliders, real-time mass/power budget calculation, and orbital parameter simulation), and GitHub / Google Workspace for hosting and documentation.
  • Design Considerations: Built as a lightweight, browser-based application with zero installation barriers so any student on a basic laptop or tablet can run simulations instantly.
